name: app-frame
title: App frame
description: An app's panel inside its card (D-047): a sandboxed frame with an opaque origin (sandbox="allow-scripts" only) on the board's panel route, at the panel's size, which talks to the board only by the panel protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0 over postMessage in MCP Apps' shape (docs/specification/apps.md § The panel protocol). The page makes the frame the first time its card is on screen and near enough to use (load), then keeps it loaded: frozen while the card is off screen or zoomed far (freeze / thaw), unloaded only for the page's cap of live panels or a state with no panel (D-050, superseding D-047 ruling 14). Until it loads, and while frozen, it is a light placeholder with the app's title.

files.core: app-frame-core.ts (createAppBridge: the handshake with the card's saved state in its host context, tools/call forwarding, vision-board/save-state, escape, host-context-changed, JSON-RPC checks and errors, the message and call caps; hostContext, hostStyles, parsePanelMessage, PROBLEM_WORDS, FRAME_CALLS; size-changed to fitHeight; no DOM), app-frame-size.ts (panelSize, panelHeight: the height a panel tells held to APP_SIZE.h.min to APP_LIMITS.toldHeight, APP_FRAME_RESIZE_EVENT; no DOM) and app-frame-state.ts (checkSave, SAVE_WORDS: the save request's check)
files.element: vb-app-frame.ts (defineVbAppFrame, VbAppFrameElement, AppFrameWiring, readLook; light DOM; the route is packages/format APP_PANEL_PATH)
files.styles: app-frame.css (scoped by the tag; tokens only; the size from --app-w and --app-h)

parts.vb-af-ph: the placeholder (aria-hidden: the card's name and the frame's title say it): the app's icon in its kind colour (vb-af-icon), its title (vb-af-title) and, while loading, 'Loading…' (vb-af-wait)
parts.vb-af-frame: the <iframe>, made by load(): sandbox="allow-scripts", src /app-panels/<id>, title the app's name, referrerpolicy no-referrer; hidden until the panel says it is ready (ui/notifications/initialized) or 1.5 s after it loaded, and while frozen

attributes.data-app: the app's id (APP_ID); the frame is made only for an id that fits, and a new one starts the panel again
attributes.data-label: the app's name: the placeholder's title and the frame's title
attributes.data-w, data-h: the panel's size in px, held to APP_SIZE (panelSize); set as --app-w and --app-h through the CSSOM; a change tells a ready panel (host-context-changed). With wire's fit (the appFit flag), the height a loaded panel tells (size-changed, panelHeight) takes data-h's place in --app-h until the frame is removed; the host context keeps data-w and data-h
attributes.data-state: idle | loading | ready (set by the element)
attributes.data-focus-in: focus is inside the panel (set by the element from the window's blur and focus: Chromium never matches :focus-within on a frame of another origin); the frame draws the focus ring unless data-pointer-focus is set
attributes.data-pointer-focus: focus came into the panel by a click (wire's focusCame said 'pointer'): no ring, as on a card; cleared when focus leaves, and the next focus by keyboard draws the ring
attributes.data-frozen: the frozen state (set by freeze(), cleared by thaw() and unload()): the panel keeps running and what it holds, its frame not painted (visibility: hidden) and the placeholder shown without 'Loading…', whatever data-state says
attributes.inert: set with data-frozen: no click, no focus and out of the tab order while frozen
attributes.aria-busy: true while loading (set by the element)

methods.wire({ callTool, saveState?, loadState?,: once: whether the panel's own height is the frame's (fit: the appFit flag; left out, its default), the page's call_app_tool through its I/O layer, the card's saved panel state (saveState keeps a save, loadState gives the value for ui/initialize; left out, a save is refused and none is given), how focus came into the panel (left out: the ring shows), the board's look (left out: readLook, the tokens resolved through a probe, the theme from the card surface), what Esc in the panel does (left out: focus the card) and what each load of the frame's document does (the panel, or the panel route's 404 once the app went: the page reads list_apps again)
methods.load(): make the frame and its protocol bridge, and listen for messages; nothing while loaded, not in the page, or for a bad id
methods.unload(): remove the frame, close the bridge, stop listening, thaw, and the height back to data-h's; focus in the panel goes back to the card; also on disconnect
methods.freeze(): a loaded panel out of use: data-frozen and inert, the frame unpainted, the placeholder shown; focus in the panel goes back to the card; nothing while unloaded or already frozen
methods.thaw(): a frozen panel back in use as it was (data-frozen and inert removed)
methods.lookChanged(): the board's theme changed: a ready panel gets host-context-changed with the parts that changed

events: message on window: passed to the bridge, as the frame's only when event.source is this frame's window and event.origin is "null"; every other window's message is ignored
ui/notifications/escape from the panel -> onEscape (focus back to the card)

vb-app-frame-resize (APP_FRAME_RESIZE_EVENT; bubbles, CustomEvent): detail { height } when the frame's height changed by itself: the panel told a new one (size-changed, with fit), or the frame was removed and the height is data-h's again. The page measures the card again
blur and focus on window while loaded: data-focus-in follows whether the frame is the page's active element
whenToUse: Inside an app card (kind app), which the node template draws it into.
whenNotToUse: Any other embedded content: Markdown never renders HTML (D-023), and nothing else on the board may run in a frame.
accessibility: The frame has a title naming the app, so a screen reader announces it on entry. Tab moves from the card into the panel and on out of it in the page's order; the panel is hidden (so not focusable) until it is ready. Esc in a panel that sends ui/notifications/escape (the example does) returns focus to the card; the board cannot see keys inside the panel, so a panel that sends none is left with Tab or Shift+Tab. The placeholder is aria-hidden; aria-busy marks the frame while it loads. Unloading or freezing a frame that holds focus moves focus to the card, never to the page's body. A frozen frame is inert: it takes no click, no focus and is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.
